findings.our_title: PARAMVAL error action dereferences parser context cleared by the nested-strategy mid-rule
findings.location: src/libscotch/parser_yy.y:458-464 (mid-rule clears context), :482-488 (error action), bison state 78 (after '=') is where error is shifted
findings.evidence: parser_yy.y:460-463: '($<SAVE>$).strat = penvptr->straptr; ($<SAVE>$).param = penvptr->paraptr; penvptr->straptr = NULL; penvptr->paraptr = NULL;'  parser_yy.y:484-486: 'errorPrint ("stratParserParse: invalid value for parameter \"%s\" of method \"%s\", ...", penvptr->paraptr->nameptr, penvptr->straptr->tablptr->methtab[penvptr->straptr->data.methdat.methnum].nameptr, ...'. Mechanism (bison --report): a syntax error inside the sub-strategy pops the stack back to state 78 (the only state that shifts `error`), discarding the $<SAVE>$ mid-rule value without restoring it; the error action then runs with NULL (or stale inner) context.
findings.review_accuracy: accurate on crash, location and reproducer. Its 'Fix' (guard NULL or restore from saved state) is only half right: a NULL guard loses the parameter name, and the saved state cannot be restored by the final action because bison has already discarded it; the restore must happen when the value is discarded (destructor) or the error rule must move inside the sub-strategy alternative. The context can also be non-NULL but stale (inner method with outer parameter), which a NULL guard does not catch.

fix_options.label: A. Typed <SAVE> mid-rule value with a %destructor that restores the context (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Give the mid-rule value a type (bison >= 3.1 typed mid-rule, CMake already requires 3.8.2) and declare '%destructor { penvptr->straptr = ($$).strat; penvptr->paraptr = ($$).param; } <SAVE>', so that whenever bison discards the sub-strategy context during error recovery or abort, the enclosing method and parameter are restored and the existing error rule prints the right names. Grammar and error rule unchanged, no conflict.
fix_options.tested: Built (0 warnings, 0 conflicts) 32/64-bit; all crash strings above now print the correct parameter/method; Mutation fuzz (repro/common/fuzz.py, 4 default strategies x 600 mutations, seed 1): pristine 2072/2400 sanitizer hits, patched 0/2400 (and 0/2400 with seed 2). check targets pass; test_strat_seq regression case added.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on bison calling destructors for popped symbols (documented since bison 1.875) and on typed mid-rule actions (bison 3.1+; the project's CMake requires 3.8.2 and last_resort files are generated by 3.8.2). Side-effecting destructor must be understood by readers (comment added). No behaviour change on valid input; messages for scalar typos unchanged.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Smallest coherent fix that keeps his single error rule and message; the same %destructor mechanism is what COR-23 needs (commit 3), so the three defects share one design: 'every discarded parser value has a destructor'. Precedent for minimal targeted grammar/lexer fixes: e1700d7 (COR-12), a94688c (COR-25).

fix_options.label: B. New PARAMSTRAT nonterminal with its own error alternative, context restored before YYERROR
fix_options.summary: 'PARAMVAL: $@ PARAMSTRAT {restore; if ($2 == NULL) YYERROR; store}', 'PARAMSTRAT: STRATSELECT | error { $$ = NULL; }'. The error is caught in the state after the mid-rule, where the saved value is still on the stack.
fix_options.tested: Built and run: all crash strings print the right parameter; BUT bison reports 1 shift/reduce conflict on token error in state 78 (PARAMVAL: error vs. reduce of the mid-rule), because both error rules are reachable there. Removing 'PARAMVAL: error' avoids the conflict but makes the scalar-typo message depend on bison default reductions and needs a second errorPrint site.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Plain yacc, no destructor; but either a grammar conflict or a duplicated message and reliance on default reductions.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He does not ship grammars with conflicts; rejected.

fix_options.label: C. NULL-guard the error action and print a generic message (first pass / review)
fix_options.summary: Test penvptr->paraptr/straptr for NULL and print 'invalid value for strategy parameter, line, column' when cleared.
fix_options.tested: Not re-run by me (first pass reports 0/2264 crashes with it); by construction it still prints misleading names when the context is stale but non-NULL ('r{sep=(m{asc=b}m{:})}').
fix_options.tradeoffs: Three lines, but two different messages for the same error class, loses the parameter name exactly when the user needs it (nested strategies), and does not address the discarded context being wrong rather than NULL.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would take a guard for a pure NULL case, but here the root cause is a discarded value; the guard hides it.

findings.notes: The last_resort generated parser files are NOT regenerated in this series: the maintainer does it himself in a separate commit at release time (38cbde4 'Update last_resort parser files for v7.0.17'), and his flex emits #line numbers one lower than the local flex 2.6.4 (identical otherwise), so a regeneration here would not be byte-identical to his. See SUMMARY.md.

findings.location: src/libscotch/arch_sub.c:393-399 (vnumnbr check under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1, and accepts 0), 445-457 (range/duplicate checks under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1), 472-475 (unchecked treetab[orgtermnum] writes), 91-94 (termnbr read without a lower bound)
findings.evidence: arch_sub.c:393-394: '#ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1' / '  if ((vnumnbr < 0) || (vnumnbr > orgtermnbr)) {'; 445-449: '#ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1' / '    if ((orgtermnum < 0) || (orgtermnum >= orgtermnbr))' / '      messptr = "archSubArchBuild: invalid vertex number in vertex list";' / '    else if (treetab[orgtermnum].domnsiz != 0)'; 472: '    treetab[orgtermnum].domnsiz = 1;              /* Here lies one terminal vertex */'; 401: '  domnnbr = 2 * vnumnbr - 1;'
findings.review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism, location and reproducer. Its 'Fix' line also asks to validate the archDomTerm() result unconditionally: for an in-range number this cannot fail in any class that has a matcher (archCmpltDomTerm, archHcubDomTerm, archMesh*DomTerm, archTleafDomTerm, archSubDomTerm, archDeco2DomTerm only reject numbers >= size), so it is an internal consistency check; patch 0002 keeps it as 'internal error (1)' in the same chain. The review missed that the debug check itself lets vnumnbr == 0 through (domnnbr = -1) and that a negative count reaches memAlloc in the loader.

fix_options.label: A. Unconditional checks in archSubArchBuild() plus count check in archSubArchLoad()
fix_options.summary: Lift the SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH1 guards (count, range, duplicate), require 1 <= vnumnbr <= orgtermnbr, fold the archDomTerm() result into the message chain as an internal error, and reject termnbr < 1 in the loader before allocating.
fix_options.tested: 32-bit and 64-bit ASan trees and SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree: repro/COR-03/run.sh (all cases rejected, no report), check_scotch_arch/_build/_deco, check_prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap/gpart*, alloc-failure sweep
fix_options.tradeoffs: O(vnumnbr) compares per build (negligible); inputs that silently corrupted memory now fail; vnumnbr == 0 is now rejected (it never worked).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: exactly what he did for the derived routine archDeco2ArchBuild (arch_deco2_build.c:604-615, unconditional, same messages) and for user-controlled sizes in 7.0.17 (c5baef9 archHcubArchLoad bound, febaef7 negative edge values); archCmpltArchLoad's 'termnbr < 1' is the model for the loader check.

fix_options.label: B. Validate in archSubArchLoad() only
fix_options.summary: After loading the inner architecture, check the count against archDomSize() and detect out-of-range/duplicate numbers with a byte flag array; leave archSubArchBuild() debug-checked.
fix_options.tested: compiled and run on the ASan tree: messages correct for sub_range/sub_toomany/sub_dup/sub_zero (the remaining sanitizer reports are the un-fixed COR-04 free path, as expected for a validation-only change)
fix_options.tradeoffs: Does not protect SCOTCH_archSub()/SCOTCH_archSub Fortran (the API crash remains); duplicates the knowledge of terminal numbering; one more allocation per load.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: would not take it: leaves the public API unprotected and diverges from archDeco2ArchBuild.

findings.notes: test_added is empty because src/check has no negative-test precedent (every test_*.c must succeed and the error library writes to stderr); a failing-call test would be a style departure, so the reproducers carry it. findings.our_title: Failed sub-architecture load frees the inner Arch twice, or frees an unset or uninitialized one
findings.location: src/libscotch/arch_sub.c:109-125 (archSubArchLoad frees the inner Arch itself, never archInit()s it), 193-198 (archSubArchFree assumes both pointers are set), 423-427 (archSubArchBuild sets the body fields before it can fail), 482-498 (Build frees only treetab on failure); src/libscotch/arch.c:215-217 (archLoad calls the class free hook after a failed load)
findings.evidence: arch_sub.c:115-121: '  o = archLoad (orgarchptr, stream);' / '  if (o == 0)' / '    o = archSubArchBuild (subarchptr, orgarchptr, termnbr, termtab);' / '  if (o != 0) {' / '    archExit (orgarchptr);' / '    memFree  (orgarchptr);'; 193-195: '  if ((archArch (archptr)->flagval & ARCHFREE) != 0) { /* If sub-architecture needs to be freed too */' / '    archFree (archptr->archptr);'; 423: '  subarchptr->archptr = orgarchptr;'; 109: '  if ((orgarchptr = memAlloc (sizeof (Arch))) == NULL) {' (no archInit() follows)
findings.upstream_change: d555f2c touched the archLoad() failure path (NULL guard only); archSubArchFree is non-NULL, so 'sub' was unaffected.
findings.review_accuracy: accurate; in my runs the 'double free' shows first as a heap-use-after-free READ in archFree (same root cause), and the 0xbebebebe class pointer reproduces exactly. Its 'Fix' line (publish on success, one owner per allocation, valid clasptr on every failure) is what patch 0001 does.

fix_options.label: A. Body owns the inner Arch from its allocation; Free is the single clean-up (patch 0001)
fix_options.summary: archSubArchLoad() NULLs archptr/termtab on entry ('Assume nothing allocated yet', as archDeco2ArchLoad2 does), archInit()s the inner Arch and stores it in the body right after allocation, and never frees it itself: archLoad() frees it through archSubArchFree(), which skips NULL pointers. archSubArchBuild() sets the body fields only on success and frees all of its data on every error path (shared tree-block loop, 'else' chained under #ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_ARCH2 as in graph_coarsen.c:331).
fix_options.tested: see 'ran': 32/64-bit ASan trees, SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree, malloc-failure sweep, check_scotch_arch/_build/_deco, check_prog_atst/amk/amk_grf/acpl/gmap/gpart*, git am on a fresh clone
fix_options.tradeoffs: Relies on archLoad() calling the class hook on failure (it does since 6.0; d555f2c kept it); a reused Arch not passed through archInit() is covered by the explicit NULLing. No ABI change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: matches d555f2c's intent (archLoad performs the clean-up), archInit()'s stated purpose (arch.c:130-132: zeroed body so class routines can test their pointers), archDeco2ArchLoad2's 'Assume nothing allocated yet' NULLing (arch_deco2_build.c/arch_deco2.c:146-148), archDecoArchFree/archTleafArchFree's NULL-tolerant frees, and his 'else' + '#endif' chaining (graph_coarsen.c:331).

fix_options.label: B. Loader cleans up after itself; Free tolerates NULL
fix_options.summary: Keep archExit()/memFree() of the inner Arch in archSubArchLoad() (after an archInit()), set archptr to NULL afterwards, NULL the fields on entry, make archSubArchFree() NULL-tolerant, and publish Build's fields only on success.
fix_options.tested: built into the ASan tree and run: sub_dup/sub_badtype/sub_badinner/sub_short/sub_var -> ret=1, 0 sanitizer hits; sub_ok loads
fix_options.tradeoffs: Works, two lines longer, two owners over the lifetime of the inner Arch (loader then body), and contradicts the hook-does-the-clean-up protocol that the other loaders follow.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: plausible but not his pattern: no loader in the tree frees what its Free hook will free.

fix_options.label: C. Build into a temporary ArchSub and copy on success
fix_options.summary: Load into a local ArchSub and memCpy it into the body only when everything succeeded.
fix_options.tested: untested: not written -- it still needs a NULL-tolerant archSubArchFree() because archLoad() calls the hook on the (zeroed) body, so it is A plus a copy
fix_options.tradeoffs: larger diff for no gain
fix_options.maintainer_fit: no precedent in arch_*.c

findings.notes: Ownership protocol applied to both meta-architectures (sub in 0001, dist in 0003): (1) the loader NULLs its pointer fields first; (2) each allocation is stored in the body as soon as it exists, after archInit() for an Arch; (3) the loader frees nothing on failure -- archLoad() calls the class free hook; (4) the hook skips NULL fields and honours ARCHFREE for the inner Arch; (5) archSubArchBuild() (also behind SCOTCH_archSub) frees everything it allocated and sets the body only on success. Groups handling deco/deco2 (COR-16) should note that archDeco2ArchLoad2 currently frees on its own 'fail:' label AND is freed again by archLoad(); under this protocol the label would go. No negative test added (no precedent in src/check).

findings.location: src/libscotch/common_file_compress.c:247-261 (fork branch), src/libscotch/common_file_decompress.c:224-238, src/libscotch/common_file.c:292-302 (fileBlockClose waits for child i before closing pipe i+1)

No new state, no list maintenance; thread implementation untouched. Test program takes an optional second output file; the check rules run a 3-file case.

findings.our_title: Thread creation failure leaves started slaves in start-up barrier; main spins forever, desctab leaked
findings.location: src/libscotch/common_thread.c:142-147 (failure path), :154 (start-up barrier), :186-191 (threadContextExit2 spin), :316 (threadWait start-up barrier)
findings.evidence: common_thread.c:143-146: 'errorPrint ("threadContextInit: cannot create thread (%d)", thrdnum); contptr->thrdnbr = thrdnum; /* Terminate all threads that have been launched to date */ threadContextExit (contptr); return (1);' -- threadWait:316 'threadContextBarrier (thrddat.contptr); /* Wait for all threads to complete initialization */' blocks the launched slaves until barrnbr == thrdnbr (original count), while threadContextExit2:187-191 spins 'while (barrnbr != thrdnbr)' with the reduced count; desctab (alloc :128) is never freed on this path and the lock/cond (:133-134) never destroyed when thrdnum == 1.
findings.review_accuracy: accurate (mechanism, both symptoms, location). Its 'Fix:' (track started threads, make shutdown independent of the start-up barrier) is the structural option B below; it is not necessary: completing the start-up barrier with the reduced count is enough and keeps the existing protocol.

fix_options.label: A. Complete the start-up barrier with the reduced count, then exit (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Under the lock set thrdnbr = thrdnum (threads launched so far + main); main joins threadContextBarrier() so the launched slaves reach their wait loop; threadContextExit() terminates them; destroy lock/cond when no slave was launched (thrdnbr == 1 makes Exit2 return at once); memFree (desctab).
fix_options.tested: repro/COR-09 FAIL_AT=1,2,3 on 32- and 64-bit ASan trees (no hang, no leak); TSan tree 0 warnings; check_common_thread, check_common_random, check_scotch_context, check_scotch_graph_map at 1/2/4 threads x SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=0/1 on both trees, all rc=0.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps the maintainer's protocol and his own intent (he already lowered thrdnbr and called threadContextExit). One special case (thrdnum == 1) because the lock features are only destroyed by Exit2 when thrdnbr > 1. The slaves' unlocked early-out read of thrdnbr in threadContextBarrier():231 can only observe 1 when no slave exists, so it is harmless (TSan agrees).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Minimal change in the shape of the existing failure path, reusing threadContextBarrier()/threadContextExit() exactly as the success path does ('Ensure all slave threads have started before cleaning-up resources', common_thread.c:154). Same style as his 7.0.17 fixes that complete an error path rather than redesign it (3c9b3ab 'Rework error handling and structure of dgraphInduce()').

fix_options.label: B. Two-phase start: slaves park on a start/abort flag, not on the barrier
fix_options.summary: New ThreadContext field strtval; threadWait() waits for strtval != 0 before the start-up barrier and exits (acknowledging) if strtval < 0; threadContextInit() sets strtval = 1 after all creations, or -1 on failure and spins on the acknowledgements; Import1 sets strtval = 1.
fix_options.tested: untested: design alternative only (applies on v7.0.17); it changes threadWait(), which also serves imported and split contexts, and adds a field to an internal structure.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Shutdown independent of the start-up barrier as the review suggests; more state, one more wake-up per thread at start, more code on the hot path of every context creation; no functional gain over A.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Larger than needed; he keeps ThreadContext minimal (a5ee23b 'Remove useless structure definition').

findings.notes: No src/check test: the defect needs an injected pthread_create failure (repro/COR-09/shim.c, LD_PRELOAD) and there is no fault-injection precedent in src/check. findings.our_title: No %destructor: strategy and test sub-trees popped on error are leaked
findings.location: src/libscotch/parser_yy.y (no %destructor; YYABORT sites :162 :182 :200 :231 :286 :290 :365 :400 :487 :502 :523 :543 :567 :600 :629 :654 :685 :700 :735 :740); nested method nodes saved at :460 are lost; stratParserParse :824-828 frees only penvdat.straptr
findings.evidence: parser_yy.y:824-828: 'if (o != 0) { if (penvdat.straptr != NULL) stratExit (penvdat.straptr); return (NULL); }' is the only cleanup; grammar has no %destructor declaration (git grep '%destructor' src -> none). Bison yacc.c skeleton: on YYABORT 'Do not reclaim the symbols of the rule whose action triggered this YYABORT' then yydestruct for every remaining stack entry, so the existing manual stratExit/stratTestExit of right-hand-side values before YYABORT (e.g. :160-161) remain required and do not double free.
findings.review_accuracy: accurate; its fix (add %destructor for the strategy and test types) is right but incomplete: it does not cover the method nodes being built (kept in penvptr->straptr / in the saved mid-rule values, not in typed stack values), and 'string value types' need no destructor (fixed-size arrays).

fix_options.label: A. %destructor for <STRAT> and <TEST>; <SAVE> destructor frees the discarded in-progress method node (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Ownership invariant: typed stack values own completed sub-trees (destructors stratExit/stratTestExit); penvptr->straptr owns the method node being built; the <SAVE> chain owns enclosing ones; the <SAVE> destructor frees the inner node before restoring the outer; stratParserParse frees whatever is left (in-progress node or completed tree after STRAT reduced). Manual frees before YYABORT stay; the debug internal-error path gets its missing stratExit ($2).
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit, 0 warnings; every leak string above is clean under LeakSanitizer; Mutation fuzz (repro/common/fuzz.py, 4 default strategies x 600 mutations, seed 1): pristine 2072/2400 sanitizer hits, patched 0/2400 (and 0/2400 with seed 2). valid strategies and all check targets unchanged.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Depends on bison destructor semantics for popped symbols and abort cleanup (documented, stable). STRAT (start symbol) stays untyped on purpose: bison destroys the start symbol on accept.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Standard bison practice, few lines, keeps his explicit frees; coherent with commit 2's destructor.

fix_options.label: B. Own the method node on the stack via a typed STRATMETHOD mid-rule value; stratParserParse no longer frees

fix_options.tested: Built and run: fixes the nested leaks but LEAKS the whole tree when the error comes after a complete strategy ('r{...}:' -> 624 bytes) because the STRAT rule has already handed the tree to penvdat.straptr, which is no longer freed; also bison -Wother 'unused value: $2'. Rejected.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cannot distinguish 'in-progress node on the stack' from 'completed tree in penvdat' at stratParserParse time.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: No.

findings.location: src/libscotch/common_thread.c:140 and :151 (coretab[i] % corenbr), :829-854 (threadProcessCoreNum, mask-based lookup used only for automatic placement), :789-795 (pthread_setaffinity_np result ignored), :810-821 (corenbr = CPU_COUNT of the saved mask)

(coretab[thrdnum] % corenbr) : threadProcessCoreNum (contptr, thrdnum);' ; :815 'corenbr = CPU_COUNT (&contptr->savedat.cpusdat);' ; :839-848 walk the saved mask for automatic placement; doc/src/scotch/s_l.tex:8179-8191 says coretab holds 'the logical indices of the cores ... subject to modulus reduction ... The conversion from logical core numbers to physical core numbers depends on the platform features'.

fix_options.maintainer_fit: Makes the code match his own documentation and INSTALL.txt (threads are placed 'within the run-time thread binding'); one lookup routine for both placements, as the comment at :152 ('slaves use saved main thread mask') already assumes.

findings.evidence: 7.0.17 common.h:321 `#define flagSet(a,n) (a)[(n)/(sizeof (int)<<3)] |= (1 << ((n)&((sizeof (int)<<3)-1)))` -- signed `int` array and `1 <<`; its users bdgraph_bipart_ex.c (movegsttab/flagloctab `int * restrict`) and bdgraph_bipart_bd.c (orgflagloctab `int *`) inherit the UB at bit 31.

fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; macro UBSan clean; check_scotch_dgraph_check passes.

findings.our_title: kgraphCost isolated-anchor block is dead code; the review's fix to enable it is incorrect
findings.location: src/libscotch/kgraph_cost.c:150-172 (dead search loop + block), 177-180 (final load-target loop)
findings.evidence: 7.0.17 :150-152 `for (...) if ((verttax[...+1]-verttax[...]) != 0) continue;` -- both outcomes continue, so domnnum always ends at domnnbr and the `if (domnnum != domnnbr)` block is unreachable; fdomwgt/fvelsum stay 0.
findings.review_accuracy: Partly wrong. The dead code is real, but the review's fix ('== 0) break;') is incorrect: an anchor with no band edge is NOT a valid 'empty part' predicate -- after the band strategy repartitions, regular vertices can be assigned to a part whose anchor has no band edge, so freezing that part's load to the anchor weight subtracts a wrong value and trips the kgraphCost debug assertion (demonstrated).

fix_options.summary: Turn the search into `==0) break;` and guard the final loop to skip isolated anchors.
fix_options.tested: Built; UNSAFE: under SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL with a default-style band mapping it fires 'kgraphCost: invalid load difference' and SEGVs, because 'anchor has no band edge' is not equivalent to 'empty part' after repartitioning.

fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would NOT take this: it activates logic whose predicate is wrong and trips his own consistency check.

fix_options.summary: Remove the unreachable search loop and freeze block and the now-constant fdomwgt/fvelsum; behaviour is unchanged (the block never ran).
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit 0 warnings; gra19 output identical to pristine; passes SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL and all check targets.

findings.our_title: Block ordering splits in vertex order, re-runs its strategy per sub-block, and drops trailing zero-load columns
findings.evidence: hgraph_order_bl.c:140 'vnodnum = grafptr->s.baseval;' and :162 'vnlosum += grafptr->s.velotax[vnodnum];' (local vertex order) while :167 'cblkptr->cblktab[cblknum].vnodnbr = vnodnum - vnodbas;' is applied to ordering positions; :172 'while (vnlosum < grafptr->vnlosum)' stops before trailing zero-weight columns; :192 'if (hgraphOrderBl (grafptr, ordeptr, ordenum, cblkptr->cblktab + cblknum, paraptr) != 0)' re-enters :96 'hgraphOrderSt (grafptr, ...)' on the whole graph for each sub-block; s_l.tex:1357-1360 'the resulting separators tree is traversed and all of the column blocks that are larger than 2 size are split ... without changing the ordering that has been computed'.
findings.upstream_change: a90b1cb (7.0.11) 'Bugfix: do not get vertex loads through inverse permutation' replaced velotax[peritab[vnodnum]] (which indexed the local load array with original vertex numbers on induced subgraphs) by velotax[vnodnum]; 7.0.17 untouched.

fix_options.label: a. Run strategy once, compute column loads in ordering order, split leaves recursively (committed)

fix_options.tested: repro/GRA-22 (7 strategies, 32/64-bit), mord twin, check_prog_gord/gord_block/gotst/mord
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two temporary arrays (n and 4n Gnums) on weighted induced subgraphs; block boundaries change for weighted graphs (intended); SEQU nodes with a single child are no longer produced.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Static '2' helper declared in the .h under the file marker (his hgraph_order_cp.h:95-97 idiom); intSort2asc1 pair matching as in mapLoad (mapping_io.c:158); behaviour is the one his manual documents.

findings.location: src/libscotch/bgraph_bipart_df.c:207-213 (goto skip), :275-284 (skip barrier and check), :356-362 (NaN branch), :387-394 (per-pass check), :519-525 (results read without any abort check)
findings.evidence: :211-212 `loopptr->abrtval = 1;\n    goto skip;` (jumps over the threadReduce at :260); :360-361 `loopptr->abrtval = 1;                   /* Threads need to halt                      */\n          vertnum = vancnnt;                      /* Skip regular computations but synchronize */` followed by :364 `difntax[vertnum] = diffval * ielstax[vertnum];`; :519 `grafptr->fronnbr      = loopdat.thrdtab[thrdlst].fronnnd[0]; /* Get data after scan-reduction */` with no test of loopdat.abrtval.
findings.review_accuracy: Accurate on the store/read past the run and on the skipped reduction (the for-loop increment leaves vertnum == vancnnt + 1, so the `vertnum == vancnnd` block is skipped) and on abrtval never being checked. The hang is real but its mechanism is not 'skips threadReduce while others wait' alone: a desynchronised thread returns to threadWaitBarrier(), which shares the barrier counter, so the usual outcome is a worker re-running the routine on freed data (stack-use-after-return) and a hang when the flag is observed late at the post-allocation check. The review's fix ('leave the loop before the store, still reach the reduction, return 1 when abrtval != 0') would turn the graceful overflow roll-back into an error and leaves the allocation-failure `goto skip` barrier mismatch and the flag races.

fix_options.label: Barrier after allocation, overflow pass stamped per thread, error returned (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Allocation failure sets the shared flag and all threads meet at a barrier right after the allocation (as bgraphBipartGa() does), then return together; the shared flag is only written before barriers, so its tests are race-free, and bgraphBipartDf() returns 1 when it is set. On overflow the thread stores the last value of its run in place (vertnum = vancnnt - 1) so no index goes out of range and the anchor reduction is still executed, and records the pass number in its thread block; after the per-pass barrier every thread aborts if some block carries the current pass number, so a faster thread that already overflowed in the next pass cannot be mistaken for the current one.
fix_options.tested: Fault injection and NaN injection as in 'ran' (c); normal runs bit-identical to pristine with 1/4/8 threads, 32- and 64-bit; check_scotch_graph_map, check_prog_gpart, check_prog_gmap, check_scotch_graph_order, check_scotch_context, check_scotch_graph_part_ovl, check_prog_gpart_overlap, check_prog_gpart_remap, check_scotch_graph_coarsen all pass with 0 sanitizer reports on the 32-bit and the 64-bit ASan+UBSan builds of the full series (logs $WORK/check_build*_*.log); check_prog_gpart, check_prog_gmap, check_scotch_context and check_scotch_graph_map also pass on a -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL build; BGRAPHBIPARTDFNOTHREAD variant compiles with -Wall.
fix_options.tradeoffs: One more barrier per call and a thrdnbr-sized scan per pass (negligible). Thread block grows by one INT. Overflow keeps returning 0 with the last valid state (unchanged behaviour); allocation failure now returns 1 instead of garbage.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same shape as his own bgraph_bipart_ga.c:151-163 (allocate, barrier, test flag, free and return) and as the review asked for the error return; the pass stamp is the cheapest way to make the per-pass test race-free without doubling barriers; his kgraph_map_df.c has the same race, so he will want one idiom for both.

fix_options.summary: Keep a single shared abort flag (1 = overflow, 2 = error) but read it into a local between two consecutive barriers after each pass, so that no thread can change it while others test it; same allocation barrier and error return as above.
fix_options.tested: untested: compiled only (gcc, ASan flags, 0 warnings); not run.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Simpler to read, but doubles the number of barriers per pass (40 passes by default, called once per bipartitioning job) and still relies on the magic values 1 and 2.

findings.our_title: Fold receiver cannot allocate edge array after senders posted; peers hang, receives undrained
findings.location: src/libscotch/dgraph_fold.c:463-466 (allocation after all sends posted), :762-773 (fail3 -> fail4 skips MPI_Waitall and frees), :798-812 (fail4: dgraphExit on arrays still targeted by Irecvs); twin src/libscotch/hdgraph_fold.c:452-456, :891-902, :925-939

findings.review_accuracy: Mechanism and lines accurate (7.0.17 lines are the 7.0.16 ones +0/+1). Its first fix (agree on allocation success before posting edge data) is the right one. Its second fix (complete every posted request at fail3) is insufficient alone: the senders' edge-data Isends have no matching receive on the failed receiver and cannot complete. 'receivers sit in MPI_Allreduce' holds only in SCOTCH_DEBUG_DGRAPH1 builds; in release builds the agreements are compiled out and peers hang in MPI_Waitany/Finalize.

fix_options.label: A: collective allocation gate before edge data is sent, unconditional first agreement, one cleanup label (recommended)
fix_options.summary: Senders post only edge-count and vertex messages; pure receivers post their count/vertex receives, wait for the counts and allocate the edge array; then all processes agree (MPI_Allreduce MAX on orggrafptr->proccomm). On failure every pending communication is matched, so one MPI_Waitall over the whole (MPI_REQUEST_NULL-prefilled) request array drains them before buffers are freed. The first agreement (fail1) is always performed and also covers graph compaction and the debug parameter checks. All error paths share one cleanup label that frees the folding data, the communication array, the compacted arrays, the folded data array and the folded graph. The debug-only agreements before dgraphCheck and at the end are kept as designed (nothing but MPI calls can fail after the gate: dgraphBuild4 does not allocate). Same restructuring in hdgraphFold2().
fix_options.tested: Fault injection on every allocation of dgraphFold2 (receiver and sender, base 0/1, np=3,4) and of hdgraphFold2 (through dgraphOrderCompute): all processes return 1, no hang, no sanitizer report. After the series: check_strat_par, check_scotch_dgraph_{check,band,coarsen,order,grow,induce,redist}, check_libparmetis_{v3,dual}, check_prog_{dgord,dgpart,dgscat-dggath,dgtst} all exit 0 on the 32-bit ASan+UBSan tree and on the 64-bit Gnum tree ($WORK/chk_32_*.log, chk_64_*.log; the only sanitizer lines are pre-existing ones in library_dgraph_coarsen.c:163 and bgraph_bipart_ml.c:195, other groups); check_scotch_dgraph_{check,coarsen,order,redist,induce} and check_prog_dgord also pass on an ASan -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL tree (chk_dbg_*.log). Zero compiler warnings in the three trees. git am of the 7 patches on a fresh clone of v7.0.17 succeeds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Two small MPI_Allreduce per fold in release builds (one before posting, one before edge data), against a data exchange of half the graph: negligible. Reverses the maintainer's explicit choice to compile the first agreement out ('cannot be merged with a useful one'); there is no existing collective to piggyback on in release builds. Function grows by ~30 lines; six fail labels instead of four. MPI call failures (fatal by default) remain unrecoverable, as before.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Uses his 7.0.17 idiom exactly: 'cheklocval = 1; /* Assume an error */', goto failN, 'cheklocval = 0; /* Everything went well */' before the agreement label, a label inside the failure block that later code jumps back to (dgraphInduce2, 3c9b3ab: fail1 inside the memAllocGroup failure block), unconditional MPI_Allreduce at the fail label (hdgraphGather, 0635547).

fix_options.label: B: receiver-side cleanup only (drain own requests, free leaks), first agreement unconditional, no gate
fix_options.summary: At fail3 the receiver waits for its own posted requests, frees the folding data and the compacted arrays, then fails; the first agreement is made unconditional.
fix_options.tested: compiles (mpicc -c, 0 warnings); not run: by construction the senders' edge-data Isends stay unmatched
fix_options.tradeoffs: Fixes the use-after-free and the leaks of the receiver only; senders of edge data to the failed receiver still block forever in their final MPI_Waitall (large messages) and the other receivers return 0. Smallest diff.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Leaves the hang the review reports; he would not take a partial fix.

fix_options.label: C: over-allocate the receiver edge array before the first agreement, no second gate
fix_options.summary: Pure receivers allocate their edge array with an upper bound (remote edges, or received vertices times degrglbmax, plus local edges) before fail1, so that nothing but MPI calls can fail after the single agreement; the array is shrunk with memRealloc once the counts are known.
fix_options.tested: compiles (mpicc -c, 0 warnings); not run
fix_options.tradeoffs: One agreement instead of two, but the bound min(edgeglbnbr - edgelocnbr, vertrcvnbr * degrglbmax) can be much larger than the exact size (star-like graphs), which defeats the purpose of folding small graphs; relies on the shrinking memRealloc never failing.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He sized this array exactly on purpose (edge counts are exchanged first); extra peak memory in the fold is what the design avoids.

Its preferred sketch has defects: (a) the gate is two separate MPI_Allreduce calls, one in the sender block and one in the receiver block, so a sender-receiver would call it twice and the others once (collective mismatch); (b) on gate failure it frees the folding data and jumps to fail4 but the compacted original arrays and *flddataptr are still leaked and the senders' Isend-error paths still skip all frees; (c) it keeps the debug-only agreement before dgraphBuild4 unchanged. The dead second-pass attempt had the right structure; I audited it against the maintainer's 7.0.17 idiom and kept it, adding the review of the threaded callers (dgraphFoldDup, kdgraphMapRbPart, hdgraphOrderNd duplicate the communicator, so the new Allreduces cannot cross between the two concurrent folds).

findings.needs_note: the hang needs a launcher that does not kill the job when a rank exits non-zero; not available (Open MPI 5 only)

first_pass.preferred_fix: Finalize before the early returns

findings.severity_note: help/version exits only produce a spurious launcher error (rc 1); the error path hangs only with launchers that do not kill the job, hence low as in the review
findings.ran: mpirun --oversubscribe -np 2 dgmap -h (and -V, '?', dgord/dgscat/dggath/dgtst -h): usage printed by every rank, then 'prterun has exited due to process rank 1 ... exited without calling "finalize"', rc=1; patched: rc=0 for all 15 paths. It left MPI_Abort as a non-preferred sketch: the PT variant of the error-exit library already calls MPI_Initialized to print the rank, so it is MPI-aware by design and the abort belongs there (the sketch also lacked the MPI_Finalized guard, needed because MPI_Initialized stays true after MPI_Finalize). It did not note that usage is printed once per rank.

  G08's tree (7.0.17 + bgraphBipartGg determinism fixes, this item unfixed): ovl t1-vs-t2=16606 t2-vs-t4=7132 ; rb 4732 / 428
  G08's tree + this patch (kgraph_map_rb_part.c, wgraph_part_rb.c): ovl 0 / 0 ; rb 0 / 0
  this series alone ($WORK/build, no GG fix): ovl 0 / 0 ; rb t1-vs-t2=0 t2-vs-t4=4304 (remaining difference is bgraphBipartGg's pass sharing, PS2-G08-1/SEP-13).
new.location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/kgraph_map_rb_part.c:315-322; src/libscotch/wgraph_part_rb.c:376-383; src/libscotch/common_context.c:283-299 (contextThreadLaunchSplit creates a second pseudo-random generator)

fix_options.label: Do not split the context when deterministic behaviour is wanted (recommended)
fix_options.summary: In kgraphMapRbPart2() and wgraphPartRb2(), read CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC and run the two sub-tasks in sequence within the same context when it is set, exactly like graphMatchInit() falls back to sequential matching.
fix_options.tested: determinism runs above (1 == 2 == 4 threads once combined with G08's GG fix; overlap path already 1 == 2 == 4 with this series alone); zero warnings on 32/64-bit; check_prog_gpart, check_prog_gpart_overlap, check_scotch_graph_map on 32/64/debug builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Deterministic mode loses the recursion-level parallelism (each sub-task still uses all threads of the context for its own threaded methods, which are sequential in deterministic mode anyway). Non-deterministic mode unchanged.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Caller-side check with the exact idiom of graph_match.c:205-225 (common_context.c cannot include context.h: the option enum is libscotch-level). 'Document that deterministic needs >= 2 threads' is not an option: the documentation already promises 'for any number of threads' and 2 and 4 threads differ as well (the split recurses).

fix_options.label: Always derive the second sub-task's generator, even when running sequentially
fix_options.summary: Make contextThreadLaunchSplit() draw the second generator and run the two sub-tasks itself when the context has a single thread, so that the pseudo-random streams are identical for every thread count without losing parallelism.
fix_options.tested: untested: changes the results of every single-threaded run (COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED results change between versions), touches the common layer used by all callers, and still requires every threaded method to be thread-count independent.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps parallelism in deterministic mode; larger behaviour change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: A design change he may prefer for 7.1, not a 7.0.x bugfix.

new.our_title: Graph loaders trust unbounded header counts, label values and HB field widths (overflow / huge alloc / hang)
new.ran: Mutation fuzzer (fuzz/tools/mutfuzz.py, seed 42, 2264 iters) on patched 32-bit ASan+UBSan build. Examples: chac '2147483647 2 000' -> memAllocGroup requested 0xfffffffe00000008 (ASan); mtx '4 4 -1' -> malloc 0xfffffffffffffff8; grf label 2147483647 -> UBSan 'vlblmax + 1' overflow at graph_io.c:306 then ~8GB indxtab alloc; rsa format '(1X,10I999999)' -> UBSan at habo:270 and near-hang on '(10I9999999999)'.
new.evidence: Chaco: 'grafptr->vertnbr = chavertnbr; grafptr->edgenbr = chaedgenbr * 2;' with no sign/range check. Mmkt: 'memAlloc (2 * linenbr * sizeof ...)' with linenbr unchecked. graph_io.c:297 'memAlloc ((vlblmax + 1) * sizeof (Gnum))' where vlblmax can reach GNUMMAX. HB format: 'number = number * 10 + *charptr - '0';' with no width bound, used as a getc loop count.

fix_options.label: Reject non-positive header object counts
fix_options.summary: Add chavertnbr/chaedgenbr and mrownbr/linenbr >= 0 checks, mirroring graphLoad's header checks.
fix_options.tested: untested: not built. Closes the negative-count wrapped-alloc cases; does not bound large positive counts.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cheap and matches precedent; a negative count already fails allocation gracefully in production, so this is clarity/DoS hardening, not a corruption fix.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches graph_io.c:131-139; but whether to add it (and any upper bound / HB width bound) is the maintainer's call.

fix_options.label: Overflow-safe integer parsing and field-width bounds
fix_options.summary: Detect overflow in intLoad()/graphGeomLoadHaboFormat() accumulation and cap HB field widths to the 80-column line.
fix_options.tested: untested: design decision. intLoad() is common_integer.c, shared by every loader and outside this group's files.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Removes the UBSan overflows and the format-width hang class, but touches common code and needs an agreed bound.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Belongs with the common I/O layer; flagged for the maintainer / common-code owners.

new.our_title: graphLoad accepted negative vertex degrees and could overflow the arc-count accumulator
new.ran: Fuzzer on pristine ASan+UBSan: grf with degree 2147483647 -> UBSan 'signed integer overflow: 6 + 2147483647' at graph_io.c:224 ('degrval += edgenum'). A negative degree was silently treated as an isolated vertex. Fixed by patch 0001 (reject degrval<0; test 'degrval > edgennd - edgenum' before adding).
new.evidence: 7.0.17: 'if (intLoad (stream, &degrval) != 1)' with no degrval<0 check, then 'degrval += edgenum; if (degrval > edgennd)' - the addition overflows before the test.

fix_options.label: Reject negative degree and test overflow before adding (recommended, committed)
fix_options.summary: Add (degrval < 0); replace 'degrval += edgenum; if (degrval > edgennd)' with 'if (degrval > edgennd - edgenum)' then add.
fix_options.tested: Built 32/64-bit (0 warnings); the UBSan hit is gone; valid graphs load; all listed check targets pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: None; folded into the GRA-04/GRA-10 commit as part of one coherent read-loop validation.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same spirit as febaef7's edloval<1 check; the twin dgraphLoadDist/Cent accumulators (dgraph_io_load.c, G20) have the same pattern and should get the same fix.

new.our_title: One unmapped vertex zeroes all load, neighbor and diameter statistics of the sequential map view
new.ran: gmtst src/check/data/m4x4.grf tgt/k2.tgt repro/PS2-G16-1/partial.map (vertex 0 absent from the map file; SCOTCH_graphTabLoad leaves it at -1), pristine 7.0.17 ASan build: 'M Processors 0/2 (0)', 'M Target min=0 max=0 avg=0 dlt=0 maxavg=0', 'M Neighbors min=0 max=0 sum=0', 'M PartDiam min=0 max=0 avg=0.000000' (comm lines are right). Patched: 'M Processors 2/2 (1)', 'M Target min=7 max=8 avg=7.5 ...', 'M Neighbors min=1 max=1 sum=2', 'M PartDiam min=6 max=7 avg=6.500000'. Also covered by src/check/test_scotch_graph_map_view (third view: Processors 2/8, Target 3/4).
new.location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/library_graph_map_view.c:302-309 (domntab built from all vertices, sorted; -1 labels sort first), 317 (loop stops at labl == ARCHDOMNOTTERM, which is -1), 383 (nghbtab[0] = -2 lets a -1 end vertex be inserted as a neighbor part)
new.evidence: 'domntab[vertnum].labl = parttax[vertnum];' for every vertex, then 'intSort2asc2 (domntab, grafptr->vertnbr);' and 'for (vertidx = 0; domntab[vertidx].labl != ARCHDOMNOTTERM; vertidx ++)' with '#define ARCHDOMNOTTERM ((ArchDomNum) ~0)' (arch.h:101): an unmapped vertex (-1) is sorted to index 0 and terminates every domain loop immediately, so mapnbr == 0. The comm loop at 462 explicitly skips '~0' vertices, and the twin SCOTCH_dgraphMapStat has a dedicated '-1' cell for unmapped vertices (library_dgraph_map_stat.c:189,194,436), so partial mappings are meant to be supported.

fix_options.summary: Skip -1 vertices when filling domntab (give them pidx ~0), sort/iterate only the mapped ones, and set nghbtab[0] = ~0 so that an unmapped end vertex always matches the sentinel in the neighbor search.
fix_options.tested: gmtst partial/full/one-vertex maps (repro/PS2-G16-1/README), test_scotch_graph_map_view 0 and 1, all check targets listed in SUMMARY.md, 32- and 64-bit.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Statistics of partial mappings change from all-zero to meaningful; full mappings unchanged (verified on the shipped check data with one thread).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors what SCOTCH_dgraphMapStat already does for unmapped vertices (its '-1' cell and 'nmskloctab[0] &= ~1'), keeps the existing TRICK sentinel style (library_graph_map_view.c:306 'TRICK: avoid testing (i+1)').

fix_options.label: B. Same filtering, explicit test instead of the sentinel trick
fix_options.summary: Identical domntab filtering, plus an explicit '(pidxend != ~0)' test in the neighbor loop.
fix_options.tested: compiles (gcc -c with the build flags); behaviour equivalent by reading
fix_options.tradeoffs: One more branch per arc; more readable than the sentinel.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Acceptable; he tends to prefer sentinel tricks over per-arc tests.

fix_options.tested: compiles
